items.title: A04: Linux ELF workload baseline, pinned rootfs and guarded differential replay
items.body:
## A04 Linux userland compatibility baseline

This draft PR records reproducible original-Linux behavior, fixed rootfs/workload inputs, fixed-commit Hepta evidence, guarded QEMU replay, and the first real Asterinas guest capability probe. It does not claim full Debian13 ELF compatibility or authenticated Hepta W1 completion.

### Current head and fixed inputs

- Branch: agents/A04-linux-hepta-baseline
- Current head: da4107f8bf525b773c8b40899f443c292c3e6dbd
- Asterinas v0.19.0: c4b7ed575b7b32773475b194d2ad41fb8d9345
- Hepta source: f8c9419df6ddeb36ff8b522a50219981fb8d9345
- Rootfs manifest SHA-256: 55aa8369d4f912267139ef7626c752814d7dc833e49accc337529f2545fb94cb
- USTAR SHA-256: df8df2e3cdcd308ef62a59268a4519e2923c9ff78145e46f26a4092725e80797
- Catalog SHA-256: 64b268956848d4fd97c6ace51343d607f20495d7bd317491a5bf7ead5e672db0

### Evidence

- Host workload tests: 87 OK / 6 managed-host skips, also under python3 -O; catalog 31 pass + 1 Tokio not_run.
- Original Linux chroot/staged C ELF: 28/28; five-round stress: 90/90; SQLite WAL source workaround passes.
- QEMU 8.2.2 and accepted SeaBIOS were extracted under /tmp only; A01 kernel/initramfs booted under TCG and exited 33.
- Guest capability probe: 13 cases, 11 pass. Pathname/abstract AF_UNIX and peer credentials pass in guest.
- Real guest gaps: MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC leaves FD_CLOEXEC clear; RLIMIT_NOFILE soft=32 still permits 256 opens without EMFILE. Evidence: tests/workloads/linux/baselines/guest-qemu-probe-20261017.json.
- Exact Debian13 package/toolchain reconstruction was attempted without system installation; all four rebuilt ELF hashes differ from the manifest. Evidence: tests/workloads/linux/baselines/exact-rootfs-input-recheck-20261017.json. The original rootfs/ELF bytes are still required.

### Hepta and remaining owners

- Fixed Hepta e2e build exited 101 with zero Wiremock Responses requests and no terminal receipt; provider audit finds zero concrete invocation-provider implementations/attachments.
- A05: fix MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC and RLIMIT_NOFILE, then rerun focused probes.
- A06: retain passing futex/thread/signal/robust-owner-death probes.
- A07: supply authenticated provider composition and independent tool-effect receipt.
- A00/A01: supply the exact rootfs tar and four manifest-pinned ELF files for full replay.

All changed files remain under compat/linux/**, support/rootfs/**, tests/workloads/linux/**; root README.md remains empty.

items.title: A10: Rust-native AI workspace host prototype
items.body:
## A10 Rust-native desktop shell

This draft PR delivers the first runnable Rust desktop shell on the Linux host path, scoped to `ui/**`, `tests/ui/**`, and `support/ui/**`. The branch was originally created from main `fb135f8`, then safely merged the newer main `8f3bb49` as two-parent commit `98f6d27`. Current pushed head: `d54f2e9382b1d0dc1c4f7b1feba9f02cfb8788a4`. Only A10-owned UI, support and test paths differ from main.

### Delivered
- Conversation-first egui shell with workspace switcher, multi-task list/detail, app launcher/cards, resource inspector, notifications, settings, and read-only console/logs.
- Rust session supervisor with bounded JSON IPC, startup flock, session-generation fencing, real child spawn/kill/wait/reap observations, and explicit pending/running/completed/failed/partial/unknown/cancel-requested states.
- Notes, Calculator, and restricted Terminal app windows. Terminal uses a fixed allowlist (`help`, `status`, `version`, `echo`, `clear`, `exit`) with no shell parsing, arbitrary child, filesystem, or network access. Boundary tests cover the 512-byte command budget, 256-byte echo output cap, and local-only clear.
- Executable shell/compositor/app/GPU lifecycle model and HOS2 read-only observation adapter under `support/ui/**`.
- Fail-closed consumer permission observation model keyed by an opaque trusted owner scope: unknown/denied/revoked/expired are denied; stale and same-revision conflicting observations are rejected; grants cannot cross workspace/trust scopes; local requests never mint grants.
- Pure Rust A08 full-display Android consumer contract model: display generation, buffer ownership/lifetime, acquire/release fences, coordinate transforms, IME composition, Back/Home, suspend/resume, destroyed and provider-failed states. It has no SurfaceFlinger/Binder/dma-buf/GPU implementation or new wire protocol.
- Wayland smoke launches Notes, Calculator, and Restricted Terminal, verifies first-frame markers, shell restart survival, cancellation/reap, and an externally killed Calculator observed as FAILED with non-successful exit detail.
- Previous source-snapshot Rust validation evidence is checked in at `tests/ui/evidence/2026-10-16-rust-validation.json`. This is historical evidence, **not a Rust test run of the latest edited head**.

### Previous source-snapshot validation (not current HEAD)
- `cargo build --manifest-path ui/Cargo.toml --workspace --bins --locked --offline`
- `cargo check --manifest-path ui/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --locked --offline`
- `cargo clippy --manifest-path ui/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --locked --offline -- -D warnings`
- UI lib/bin tests: 45 passed.
- `cargo test --manifest-path support/ui/Cargo.toml --locked --offline`: 26 passed.
- `cargo test --manifest-path tests/ui/Cargo.toml --locked --offline`: 8 passed.
- Rustfmt, Bash syntax, and diff checks pass.
- Full UI all-targets reaches 45 unit/bin passes but `ipc_reconnect` is blocked in this sandbox because AF_UNIX/socket creation returns `EPERM`; an independent Python probe confirms the same kernel restriction.
- The configured cloud container has no Weston, wayland-info, Xwayland, Fcitx5/IBus, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `/dev/dri`, or `/sys/class/drm`; package installation is blocked by container privileges. Therefore no live Wayland/IME/GPU evidence is claimed.
- The previous GitHub Actions host run completed: source guard, pinned Rust build/tests, AF_UNIX reconnect, and Weston smoke passed; its final offline metadata gate failed because an Android-only locked package was not cached. `tests/ui/check-host.sh` now runs locked `cargo fetch` before that offline gate. A new run is queued to verify the fix.

### Latest incremental source (pending current-head CI)
- `98f6d27`: non-destructive merge of latest main and A10 tree, parent heads recorded in Git.
- `c42459f`: expose focus state in Notes/Calculator, remove implicit Enter-to-run from Restricted Terminal to avoid Chinese IME candidate selection executing a command; reject >512-byte commands **before** adding user input to the terminal log. Added large UTF-8 paste regression and focused IME acceptance steps.
- `d54f2e9`: normalize UI formatting and explicitly scope the earlier host evidence in docs. Root README remains zero bytes.
- GitHub Actions latest current-head run: https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/actions/runs/38986430370 (**queued**, no pass claimed). The earlier run https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/actions/runs/38932065166 built and tested the host Rust binaries and executed the Weston lifecycle step, but its final Cargo offline metadata gate failed due to an uncached Android-only locked package. The lock prefetch fix was committed later.
- No live Chinese candidate-window/real compositor restart, per-domain Xwayland, A05 portal, A07 Hepta owner or A08 Android display has been verified on the latest head.

### Follow-up interfaces
- A05/A00: authenticated process/capability identity, workspace trust domains, portal grant/revoke/expiry/unknown states, trusted prompts, and notification provenance.
- A07/A02: read-only Hepta task projection with K/D references, executor/trust-domain, revision/provenance, and owner-confirmed effect state.
- A08/A09: negotiated SurfaceFlinger full-display lifecycle and real buffer/fence/GPU import/reset evidence before APK-level windows.

The PR remains draft until the queued host CI and separately scoped Wayland/IME/compositor gates produce evidence.

items.title: A01: build pinned Asterinas and retain actual QEMU input snapshots
items.body:
This PR vendors the complete pinned Asterinas v0.19.0 derivative under the single `kernel/asterinas/` root, retaining upstream source, documentation, licenses and attribution. The developer build entries invoke upstream `make kernel` and `make run_kernel` with a small initramfs. The pin remains `c4b7ed575b7b32773475b194d2ad41fb6d03765b`, Rust `nightly-2026-07-21`; root README is zero bytes and this phase changes no kernel/core/OSTD source.

The latest fixes complete early `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS` presence rejection across the four build/test/debug/integration entries, including an empty value, before consuming outputs or tools. QEMU now loads retained private copies of its actual kernel/initramfs inputs, verified before and after execution. Source-path metadata and original argv remain available. Actual main `bc294f75bfb8c03d9963f5a12ea23b9589779d96` was integrated through merge `be86dc41228078b4b941b8a2e4d745fc09453d11`; its approved owner code was imported unchanged.

| Validation | Actual result and scope |
| --- | --- |
| New debug/integration entry guards | 56 passing host executions across isolated ordinary/optimized Python; original red assertions and old/fixed CLI probes retained. |
| QEMU input snapshots | 52 passing host executions; original checker unchanged; replacement failure retained. |
| TCP/GDB OSDK matrix at `071dd8edcd2a3cf9b33dbbeab713428317b9b76c` | 22/22, eleven real QEMU guests raw33, one VMX soft skip. Explicit TCP profile; no default-UNIX or coverage-percentage claim. |
| Full Asterinas Rust-entry debug at `31170ffb2ab6d18a85051d426e5d85a83f1b2abf` | GDB PC and 32 live instruction bytes match `__ostd_main`; detach followed by complete initramfs boot, raw33. x86_64/q35/TCG, one vCPU, 512 MiB; independent fresh live-artifact checker exit0. |
| Current-main host validation | 83 Rust passes, including one doctest, plus 98 Python passes = 181 executions. Both fmt and control strict Clippy exit0. ABI strict Clippy exits101 in three test helpers: overall validation remains partial. |
| A02 isolated candidate | Three-helper patch passes fixed-nightly 61 tests, fmt, no_std target check and strict Clippy. Its 14 inputs match current main and fresh apply-check exits0. Pending A00/A02 adoption; owner source remains unmodified. |

The successful debug run reused the DWARF artifact actually produced at `071dd8ed...`, with zero new compiling lines. It is a cached debug retry, not a fresh-target rebuild. Earlier clean-target source builds, normal boots and OSTD/core regressions keep their original source bindings and denominators. No Linux host or ISO-installer boot is counted as kernel acceptance.

The actual QEMU-loaded successful debug ELF is 5,975,720 bytes, SHA256 `fbe81c0e2deae705d61d77ccaaf604e2bf1ca30e4541de71d263af6ecc62ec1b`. Complete serial/GDB/commands, actual boot snapshots, original failed attempts, coverage counters, checksum/member indexes and the full 111 MB symbol ELF are retained. The symbol gzip is stored losslessly as 13 ordered chunks with reconstruction verification.

Review/replay:
- [Current-main validation report](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/blob/agents/A01-asterinas-boot/support/build/evidence/2026-10-16-cloud-main-sync/REPORT.md)

Remaining work includes supported KVM/VMX execution for the three earlier VMX/EPT skips; host AF_UNIX EPERM blocking two default-profile cases; cross-path/cross-host reproducibility and an immutable environment; unknown external artifact writer attribution; historical A04 two fd-limit failures/two SCM_RIGHTS timeouts; and A05/A06/A07 native G1/G2/runtime/Hepta owner integration. Infrastructure validation does not establish those features. Failed debug/OSDK attempts and all strict-Clippy diagnostics remain failures in their original evidence. Queued remote CI is not green.

Published head: `01a344c6a293fd73b158e9e6ca93bd9904b69bbf`. Integrated main: `bc294f75bfb8c03d9963f5a12ea23b9589779d96`. This PR targets main from `agents/A01-asterinas-boot`; A00 retains merge ownership.

items.title: A03: add host-model HOS2 control state core
items.body:
## Problem

The repository had only the HOS2 0.3 specification and a sequential Python model. A05/A06/A07 had no reusable Rust state core for CapSpace delivery, resource CAS, or bounded history.

## Change

- Add `libs/os-control`, an std-only Rust host model for:
  - boot/CapSpace/D identity and strict global sequence reservation
  - canonical request binding, cross-target dedupe, publisher fencing
  - immutable terminal results, QueryDelivery, DeliveryView, history_lost, and contiguous RetireThrough
  - ResourceDomain stable object identity, revision CAS, fixed 100ms CPU budgets, usage retention, parent constraints, revoke/commit ordering, and explicit pause state
- Add `tests/control/control_conformance.rs` with negative, capacity, 10,000-write, and std-thread interleaving tests.
- Add `API_CONTRACT.md` for A05/A06/A07 integration boundaries.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --manifest-path libs/os-control/Cargo.toml --all -- --check`
- `cargo test --manifest-path libs/os-control/Cargo.toml`: 1 unit test + 17 integration tests passed; 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy --manifest-path libs/os-control/Cargo.toml --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: passed.
- All evidence is Linux host-model evidence. No HOS2 wire fields, `tests/golden`, kernel source, or Hepta persistent database were modified.

## Explicit limits

This PR does not claim native kernel capability. Real ioctl credentials/copyout faults, Asterinas locking/IRQ/runqueue behavior, scheduler accounting, fsync/power-loss recovery, and durable K↔D integration remain A05/A06/A07 work.

items.title: A03: harden HOS2 control core and add portable one-shot kernel handoff
items.body:
## Result

This PR supplies the A03 Rust state core for A05/A06/A07 integration. It keeps global CapSpace delivery identity D, immutable terminal outcomes, bounded contiguous history retirement, original-owner authority, ResourceDomain CAS/accounting and the original durable Hepta K identity separate.

- Branch: `agents/A03-control-core`
- Latest main incorporated: `bc294f75bfb8c03d9963f5a12ea23b9589779d96`
- Tested code commit: `bb42cb691e6de33b8f788c94ea715bf648ff56ed`
- Current evidence HEAD: `51327db35f6e51c1818b59274275a022b7248efc`; source hashes are unchanged from the tested code commit.
- Diff against main is confined to `libs/os-control/**` and `tests/control/**`. README remains 0 bytes; no HOS2 wire/golden or other owners' sources changed, no second Hepta database, no Ollama.

## Concrete changes

A descendant previously could observe BOOTTIME T and a parent or sibling later accept an operation before T. One shared family clock floor now fences stale sampling, CAS and charges, without advancing time on failed operations or refunding consumed quota. The 12 new resource regressions run against the old code produce **4 passed / 8 expected failures**, and all 12 pass after the fix.

`execute_reserved(token, publisher, callback)` provides the synchronous external mutation seam. The reserved result slot fences namespace loss while the callback checks real authority and applies the real resource mutation under its own lock. Callback unwind or malformed metadata stays pending, blocks retirement and cannot execute again; trusted externally fenced reconciliation may later publish the result. Host `commit` uses the same seam.

The default std and optional alloc-only `portable-spin` backends share the same transitions. The no_std backend builds an `x86_64-unknown-none` rlib. It is not an IRQ/preemption-safe Asterinas adapter; locking and allocation must be integrated by the kernel owners.

Additional adversarial tests fill the real 1024-entry window behind a hanging first reservation, verify query/retirement at exhaustion, then continue to 10,000 writes in the same namespace. They also exercise wrong publishers, same-token commit/refusal, copyout-model retries, history loss, query/retirement and one-shot callback races.

## Actual validation

A clean detached checkout of the exact tested code commit passed:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| std Rust suite | **113 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored** |
| portable-spin Rust suite on host | **113 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored** |
| fmt | pass |
| strict Clippy, both backends | pass |
| x86_64-unknown-none check and rlib build | pass |
| existing A05 Linux host smoke | pass; QueryAbi, 16 malformed frames, ENOTTY vs injected EFAULT |

The same 113 test functions execute against two backends; this is 226 executions, not 226 distinct scenarios. Counts per backend: 6 unit + 81 conformance + 6 delivery adversarial + 12 resource adversarial + 8 synthetic kernel-handoff tests.

Reproduce:
```sh
sh tests/control/run-validation.sh /tmp/a03-validation
cargo build --locked --manifest-path libs/os-control/Cargo.toml --no-default-features --features portable-spin --lib --target x86_64-unknown-none
```

Full commands, regression oracle, hashes and captured logs: [tests/control/VALIDATION.md](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/blob/agents/A03-control-core/tests/control/VALIDATION.md).

## Concurrency and integration boundaries

Both backends run actual Rust thread interleavings, including same-D reservation, revoke/commit, ancestry quota, release/acquire publication visibility, pending-prefix exhaustion and retirement/query/loss. New tests include 128 commit/refusal races, 32 rounds of eight wrong publishers, 128 retry/commit/loss races, 64 retire/query/loss rounds with 128 observations each, 64 family clock races and 64 rounds of eight competing callbacks.

This is **host-model evidence**, not loom/exhaustive scheduling or actual kernel acceptance. Arbitrary schedules, weak-memory architectures, real IRQ/runqueue/preemption, SMP migration, copyout faults, asynchronous effects, crash/reboot and fsync/power-loss cuts remain unverified.

- **A05:** `try_with_capacity`, `with_capacity_for_owner`, `DeliveryRequest::from_wire`, `reserve_or_get`, `execute_reserved`, `query_delivery`, `retire_through`; bind actual CapSpace/process-start/exec epoch, credentials, leases, slot generation, history rights and copyin/copyout.
- **A06:** `RequestBinding`, `PublishOutcome`, `BudgetReceipt`, `ResourceDomain::{grant,revoke,try_usage,install_budget_for_host_model,charge_interval_for_host_model}`; use the single real ResourceDomain owner and settle runtime under its actual mutation lock.
- **A07:** value-only `LogicalOperationId(scope_id,operation_id)` / `OperationBinding(K,D)`, `HistoryAck`, `OriginalOwnerAuthority`; authenticate/fence owner replacement, persist/fsync in the existing owner and confirm only a durable contiguous terminal prefix.

Contract: [libs/os-control/API_CONTRACT.md](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/blob/agents/A03-control-core/libs/os-control/API_CONTRACT.md). The current kernel and real Hepta owner do not yet consume this crate. A05/A06/A07 G1/G2 blockers remain open for their owners; ready for review here means the scoped A03 source and host acceptance, not completed native integration.

## A00→A03: prevent malformed QueryDelivery from becoming a false success

**Owner branch base:** [A03 #50](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/pull/50) HEAD `fec6af91c5223d6efc4bb8598021e3134e9baac7`; this Draft head is `8f70353977d960243db41a0651043032a520616c`. The branch was reconciled with A03's concurrent publisher binding, namespace-slot fencing and view-right hardening via an explicit two-parent, **no-force** merge; no owner branch was overwritten. No shared HOS2 wire layout, Hepta persistence, Asterinas kernel file, fixed pin or root README changed.

### Actual bug

#50 introduced `DeliveryObservation::hos2_saved_status_code() -> u16`. Because `DeliveryObservation` has public fields, an A05 wire adapter can encounter `state=Terminal,status=None` (or nonterminal with `status=Some(Ok)`). The current helper returned **numeric 0/Ok** in either case, silently turning an invalid/unknown terminal effect into a success. It also ignored leftover terminal metadata on nonterminal states. The HOS2 QueryDelivery contract explicitly forbids that ambiguity.

### Fix / authored regressions

- Change the helper to **`Result<u16, DeliveryError>`**. Reject terminal observations without saved status; reject nonterminal observations with any saved status or effect metadata; validate successful terminal status has a nonzero stable object, complete result fields and `saved_revision == previous_revision + 1`; terminal errors require absent effect metadata.
- Preserve `Ok(0)` for valid nonterminal history states and genuine successful terminal results, and return the canonical saved error code for actual terminal denials.
- Update original A03 host conformance assertion and add three adversarial Rust tests: all four nonterminal states with malformed status/metadata; false terminal Ok, malformed revision/zero ID, real committed terminal success and real immutable denied result.
- Preserve the original model's owner/namespace and terminal linearization behavior; add no new owner authority or second K ledger.

### Verification boundary

Actual GitHub source comparison shows this Draft is **ahead of A03 by four commits, behind by zero**, changing only the two files above. The exact merged Rust source/test blobs are `a1787ed9845133bf1fbdbed8252d660074d068c1` and `90dc8bc0c7c9fe88bce41f2bfa5bf88a1c054b38`. items.title: A03: close resource lifetime and history observation blockers
items.body:
## Result

Follow-up to merged #50. A child ResourceDomain previously left a permanent parent-cap constraint after its final reference was destroyed. A delayed synchronous callback could also make one history query block the whole CapSpace table. Resource ancestry was bounded only by 65,536 lifetime identities, permitting recursive destruction to overflow a small host stack.

- **Branch:** `agents/A03-control-core`
- **HEAD:** `c2d696d8234ae274c6c5f31c1980ff9b3f8077fe`
- **Latest main incorporated:** `acd9ee30d51c405b32a36ff02ce25a9272b65834`
- **Clean-checkout tested code:** `b671c42ac8006abcf6290abbe64197e4c488f7b6`. The subsequent merge/evidence commit changes no Rust inputs; source hashes are retained.
- Scope against current main: only `libs/os-control/**` and `tests/control/**`. Main's newly added A02 pinned-host workflow is preserved. README remains 0 bytes; wire/golden and other owners' code are unchanged.

## Fixes

1. `ResourceDomainInner::drop` releases the immediate parent's active-child cap metadata at final strong-reference destruction. Clones, grants, descendants, retained terminal slots and tokens still preserve the constraint. Identity tombstones, CPU consumption and clocks are not refunded.
2. Independent per-slot execution gate and short state mutex permit query/retire/audit while a callback is paused. Namespace loss closes admission, releases the table lock, waits/fences callbacks and only then completes loss. Concurrent loss callers serialize without blocking namespace readers. Terminal results never regress to Reserved.
3. `MAX_RESOURCE_DEPTH=64`, including root, bounds traversal and recursive destruction. Deeper creation returns Exhausted before consuming identities or child metadata.

The fixes were pushed as verified code commits `7c07dc5` and `b671c42`, followed by current-main integration and evidence `c2d696d`.

## Actual validation

Reproduce with pinned `nightly-2026-07-21`:
```sh
sh tests/control/run-validation.sh /tmp/a03-validation
cargo build --locked --offline --manifest-path libs/os-control/Cargo.toml --no-default-features --features portable-spin --lib --target x86_64-unknown-none
```

A clean detached checkout passed **129/129 tests per backend**, std and portable-spin, with 0 failed/ignored/filtered. Both strict Clippy runs, fmt, bare-target check and no_std rlib build passed. Counts per backend: 6 unit, 81 conformance, 6 delivery adversarial, 8 handoff, 12 resource adversarial, 10 lifecycle and 6 nonblocking-history tests. This is 258 executions of 129 functions, not 258 distinct scenarios.

Negative evidence:
- Original 8 lifecycle regressions: **0 passed / 8 failed** before fix.
- Initial 5 history-liveness regressions: **1 passed / 4 failed** before fix.
- Depth-limit regression failed before enforcement.
- Isolated old-source 1024-parent destruction on a 64KiB stack: **SIGABRT / exit 134**; 64/128/256 controls completed. Maximum supported-depth destruction now passes.

New concurrency checks use gated callbacks and always release/join workers before assertions. They cover pending query, unrelated reservation, retirement, audit, admission closing, complete terminal observation, two simultaneous loss operations/two callbacks and 64 last-child-drop versus parent-CAS races. The existing hanging-prefix/full-1024-window and same-namespace 10,000-write cases remain passing.

[Full acceptance, commands and hashed logs](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/blob/agents/A03-control-core/tests/control/VALIDATION-20261017.md).

items.title: A06 WIP: enforce N0 CPU bandwidth through shared scheduler and cgroup
items.body:
First real kernel implementation attempt, intentionally DRAFT until pinned Rust compilation and the previously committed Asterinas guest CPU probe pass.

Changes (exact source in branch):
- Extend existing cgroup CPU controller with TSC-based period/runtime accounting, ancestor checks and throttle counters. Reconfiguration preserves already-used runtime.
- Charge the common ClassScheduler current task on scheduler events; test eligibility in both real-time and fair queues; park throttled tasks and restore them from local idle ticks. Reuse cgroup state, not a parallel HOS2 ledger. No scheduler hot-injection or model calls.
- Small A01 build-tool correction: remove `make --version | head -1` / `gcc --version | head -1` pipes under `set -o pipefail` after observing SIGPIPE 141 before any kernel compilation.

**Not claimed:** verified CPU enforcement, SMP correctness, parent/scheduler migration correctness, kernel build, Hepta effects, or API stabilization. We will retain raw build/boot/probe evidence, fix compile and semantic issues here, and not merge if regressions exist. Work is restricted to disposable QEMU and isolated source worktree; no production host cgroup, disk, services or firmware changed. Root README remains 0 bytes.

Baseline failing case in merged tests: 1% `cpu.max=1000 100000` written/read back but guest still used ~998ms CPU per 1000ms wall. Success requires low actual CPU consumption, bounded error and no deadlocks/panics in the **modified** kernel with independent probe.
